hypotheses: In the loop list, the evaluate loop is one row per evaluate run still going: the task and the model, what the run measures as what is to be achieved, the round it is at of the rounds asked, the problems it filed, and what is left. A run that stopped on a held merge says why. A run that ended is not listed; its score stays in its run folder.

given plumb evaluate simple with two fix rounds asked, in its first fix round, when the loops are listed, then its row reads simple, the model, round 1 of 2, the problems filed so far, and the fix round and the rerun as left
given an evaluate run stopped because the merge of a fix is held, when the loops are listed, then its row says it stopped and why
given an evaluate run that ended with its score written, when the loops are listed, then it is not listed
records.premise:
/plumb:plumb intent I want to improve the way we can track with plumb each debug and intent loop. from any plumb session related to a given project, I want to be able to track each intent loop and their progress, remaining actions, and also show a description of what is supposed to be achieved. Same for the debug loop and the evaluate loop

Question: This project already holds 10 intent loops on disk, 7 of them opened in October by sessions that are gone (some finished elsewhere, some abandoned). What should the list show for a loop nobody is working on any more?
Options: Show as idle, apart (Recommended) (Loops with a live session come first; loops with no session are kept below, marked 'idle since <date>', so nothing is lost and a new session can still take one over. Nothing is deleted by the list.); Only loops being worked on (The list holds only loops with a live session. Abandoned loops vanish from view (they stay on disk), so the list is short but a forgotten loop is never seen again.); Idle ones, with a way to close (As the first option, and the pane also lets you close an idle loop for good from the list. This makes the list act, not only show.)
Answer: Show as idle, apart (Recommended)
